notes: The app can now update itself: Settings checks for a new version, downloads it and installs it. The Autopilot page controls the AI's moves, and the AI shows a mood strip with the NULL mascot. Stem buttons only work when real stems are ready.
Stems for the song that is playing now load in the background and switch on while it plays, so stem moves work without waiting for the next song.

Album art is fetched from the server and kept on the phone, and the cover fades along with the mix. New History tab to replay or like past songs, and you can flag a bad pairing so it is not mixed again. More one-tap moves: filter loop, drums only, line swap and acapella build.

Smarter checks before a mix starts, with a fallback to a normal-length mix when the key clashes. You can save a transition recipe, plan a set from your own picks and save the set you played. Fixed a crash when the player was closed in the middle of a mix.
New deck tools: tap tempo, roll, brake, reverse, a level meter per deck and a 16-step beat grid for the sampler. Some old unused code was removed.
The phone now uses the same tuning values as the web player and reads the live settings from the server when it starts.

Your server library is now the home of the app and the pool for AI mixes. Big step toward matching the web player: bridge paths to a chosen next song, every AI move on demand, effects bar, deck view with sampler pads, and a Punjabi style profile. Songs are cached on the phone and resume if a download stops. You can sign in with your browser. Android Auto gets a browse tree, search and controls like skip and mix now.

Echo is now a normal effect you set yourself, separate from the AI's own echo. Per-deck key lock, a Play this transition button on the AI sheet, and you can search for a destination song that is not in your library. Android Auto shows the album art.
Up next queue, queue a song by voice, a Like button and cover pictures in the car's browse lists. Android Auto is steadier when starting, stopping and skipping quickly.
Updates download much less: the app fetches only what changed since your version and checks it, falling back to the full download if needed.
When you pick a song by hand, the AI re-anchors to it: the old booking is cancelled and the mood and style follow your choice.
New Romance mode and a sleep timer that fades out the last song. Both are chips on the now-playing screen.

Calmer now-playing screen: one row for the mix and a single mood control, plain-word reasons when the AI declines a move, and generated covers with initials. Android Auto gets steering controls, Moods and For you lists. New launcher icon. Song titles with an artist prefix or a release year are cleaned up.
Withdrawn: this version did not open. Fixed in parity.18.
Safe rollback to the parity.15 behaviour after parity.16 failed to open. No new features.

The start-up problem is fixed, and whole-song stems are back. If the app ever fails to start repeatedly it now shows a recovery screen, reports the problem and can force an update. New look foundations with the Inter and Space Grotesk fonts.
Fixed the library header and mini player showing the song list through them.

Redesign: calmer now-playing screen, AI card and mini player. Settings are regrouped, with a simple or expert DJ style and three presets. Android Auto cards show both covers, with a new icon set and sentence-case wording.
Stems load faster: each stem is one resumable download with progress, nothing is uploaded for songs the server already has, and the next two songs are fetched early.
Songs the AI picks now resolve to the right recording: the artist, exact title and length are checked, and a download that does not match is set aside.
